en: to cool down, to get cold

examples.en: My coffee has gone cold.
If the soup gets cold, heat it up again.
Rice doesn't taste good once it gets cold.

examples.ko: 배달 음식이 다 식어서 전자레인지에 데웠어요.
examples.en: The delivery food had gone cold, so I heated it in the microwave.
It's still hot. Eat it when it cools down a little.

explain: ‘국이 식어요’처럼 뜨거운 것이 차가워질 때 써요. ‘식은 밥’, ‘식은 커피’처럼 ‘식은’ 모양도 자주 써요.

dict_examples.en: He was lost in deep thought, not even noticing the soup with rice was getting cold.

dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: Use it when something hot loses its heat: 국이 식어요. The form 식은 is also very common, as in 식은 밥 (cold rice) and 식은 커피 (cold coffee).

examples.en: When ramyeon cools down, the taste changes.
This neighborhood has changed a lot.
The weather changes often, so I brought an umbrella.
My friend hasn't changed at all.
If you change your mind, please tell me.

explain: 변하다는 시간이 지나서 달라지는 거예요. 전화번호나 시간표처럼 하나가 다른 것이 될 때는 ‘바뀌다’를 써요.

dict_examples.en: Snow turns to rain.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.en: The young prince turned into a beast.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.en: The clouds were turning black.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.en: The trembling voice turned into sobbing.

explain_en: 변하다 is for things that become different over time. When one thing is replaced by another, like a phone number or a timetable, use 바뀌다.

dis.h: become different on its own; everyday word

p.n: 변화하다 sounds more formal and abstract for simple weather.

examples.en: When your bowl is empty, wash it right away.
The fridge is completely empty.
The office is empty on weekends.
My glass is empty. More water, please.
If a seat frees up on the bus, sit down.

explain: ‘컵이 비었어요’처럼 지금 상태를 말할 때 과거형을 써요. 사람이 비우면 ‘비우다’예요: 컵을 비워요.

dict_examples.en: an empty bowl
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.en: It is lunchtime, so the office is completely empty.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.en: The guard room was empty, so I couldn't leave the key.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 아무것도 안 먹어 지금 속이 텅 비어 있는 상태이다.
dict_examples.en: I haven't eaten anything, so my stomach is completely empty.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: For the present state you use the past form: 컵이 비었어요 means “the cup is empty (now)”. When a person empties it, use 비우다: 컵을 비워요.

en: to fall, to drop; to fail (a test)

examples.en: My wallet fell on the stairs.
I failed my driving test.
My phone fell on the floor.
Leaves fall in autumn.
When the temperature drops, I wear thick clothes.

explain: ‘시험에 떨어지다’의 반대말은 ‘붙다’예요: 시험에 붙었어요 = 합격했어요. 쌀이나 돈이 다 없어질 때도 ‘떨어지다’를 써요.

phrases.example: 그 말을 듣고 정이 뚝 떨어졌어요.
phrases.en: to be turned off by someone; to lose affection
phrases.nuance_ko: 좋아하던 마음이 갑자기 없어질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: used when your fondness for someone suddenly disappears
phrases.en_equiv: to be turned off by someone; to lose affection

dict_examples.ko: 굵은 빗방울이 머리에 한두 방울씩 떨어지기 시작했다.
dict_examples.en: Big raindrops began to fall on my head one or two at a time.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.en: He missed his footing and fell into a pit.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 우산 가장자리로 빗물이 좌락좌락 떨어져 내리고 있었다.
dict_examples.en: Rainwater was streaming down off the edge of the umbrella.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: The opposite of failing a test (시험에 떨어지다) is 붙다: 시험에 붙었어요 means “I passed”. 떨어지다 is also used when you run out of something, like rice or money.

dis.h: drop down from a height; fail a test

p.n: 넘어지다 is for a person or thing tipping over, so it does not fit an apple dropping from a tree.

examples.en: If a typhoon comes, be sure to close the windows.
A typhoon hit, so flights aren't taking off.
A typhoon will come tomorrow.
A typhoon is coming, so I'm staying home.

examples.ko: 태풍이 언제 와요? — 내일 저녁에 와요.
examples.en: When is the typhoon coming? — It comes tomorrow evening.

explain: 한국에서는 태풍이 보통 여름 끝에서 가을에 많이 와요. ‘허리케인’과 같은 종류인데, 아시아에서는 ‘태풍’이라고 해요.

dict_examples.en: the place where a typhoon passed
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.en: This typhoon was really terrible.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.en: A typhoon is moving north toward our country.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: In Korea, typhoons mostly come from late summer into autumn. It is the same kind of storm as a hurricane, but in Asia it is called a 태풍.

examples.ko: 태풍이 오면 길이 막힐 수 있어요.
examples.en: If a typhoon hits, the roads may get jammed.
My nose is stuffed up, so I can't smell anything.
I was late for the appointment because of traffic.
The sink is clogged, so the water won't drain.
I got a sudden question and was lost for words.

explain: 길, 코, 변기처럼 지나가야 하는 곳이 닫히면 모두 ‘막히다’예요. ‘차가 막혀요’와 ‘길이 막혀요’는 같은 뜻이에요.

phrases.example: 사무실 분위기가 너무 무거워서 숨이 막혀요.
phrases.en: to feel suffocated; to be stifling
phrases.nuance_ko: 실제 숨뿐 아니라 답답하고 힘든 분위기에도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: used for real breathlessness and also for a heavy, stifling atmosphere
phrases.en_equiv: to feel suffocated; to be stifling

dict_examples.en: The road is jammed.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.en: The passage is blocked.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.en: The drain is clogged, so the water doesn't go down.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.en: Sunlight is blocked.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.en: The river flow is blocked.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: Anything that should let things pass through, like a road, a nose or a toilet, can be 막히다 when it gets blocked. 차가 막혀요 and 길이 막혀요 mean the same thing.

dis.h: clogged or jammed; everyday physical obstruction

p.n: 차단되다 means someone deliberately shut the road, not a jam.

examples.en: I lost my wallet at the subway station last week.
I got lost, so I checked a map app.
I caught a cold and lost my appetite.
I failed the test and lost my confidence.
The company closed and I lost my job.

explain: 물건을 놓고 오거나 없어졌을 때는 ‘잃어버리다’를 더 많이 써요: 지갑을 잃어버렸어요. 잃다는 입맛, 자신감, 길 같은 말과 잘 써요.

phrases.example: 사고가 난 다음에 안전 교육을 하면 소 잃고 외양간 고치는 거예요.
phrases.en: to lock the barn door after the horse has bolted
phrases.nuance_ko: 일이 잘못된 뒤에 준비해도 늦었다는 속담이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: a proverb meaning it is too late to prepare after things have gone wrong
phrases.en_equiv: to lock the barn door after the horse has bolted

dict_examples.en: to lose money gambling
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 이번 경기마저 잃으면 본선 진출은 힘들다.
dict_examples.en: If we lose even this match, advancing to the finals will be hard.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.en: to lose a bag
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: For a lost object, 잃어버리다 is more common: 지갑을 잃어버렸어요. 잃다 goes well with things like appetite, confidence and your way.

dis.h: lose something, even abstract like trust

p.n: Both work. 잃어버리다 stresses that you carelessly lost it and cannot find it; 잃다 also covers abstract things like trust.

examples.en: I often forget things.
I forgot my password for the website.
I'm sorry, I forgot our appointment.
I forgot my friend's birthday.
Forget about bad things quickly.

explain: 잊어버리다는 ‘완전히 잊었다’는 느낌이에요. 친구하고는 ‘까먹었어’라고도 많이 말해요.

dict_examples.ko: 그는 먹는 것도 잊어버리고 공부에만 몰두하였다.
dict_examples.en: He forgot even to eat and was absorbed only in studying.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 아이는 정신없이 노느라고 배고픈 것도 잊어버렸다.
dict_examples.en: The child was playing so hard that he forgot he was hungry.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 나는 졸업한 지 오래되어서 학교에서 배운 것을 다 잊어버렸다.
dict_examples.en: It has been a long time since I graduated, so I forgot everything I learned in school.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: 잊어버리다 has the feeling of “forgot it completely”. With friends, people also often say 까먹었어.

p.n: 까먹다 is more casual and colloquial.

examples.ko: 한 학생이 계단에서 제 지갑을 주웠어요.
examples.en: A student picked up my wallet on the stairs.
I picked up trash in the park.
I picked up a thousand won on the street.
A pen fell. Please pick it up for me.
The kids pick up pretty stones at the beach.

explain: 줍다는 ㅂ 불규칙이에요: 주워요, 주웠어요. 춥다 → 추워요, 눕다 → 누워요와 같은 모양이에요.

dict_examples.en: to pick up trash
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.en: to glean ears of grain
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.en: I picked up twigs and made a campfire.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: 줍다 is a ㅂ-irregular verb: 주워요, 주웠어요. It changes like 춥다 → 추워요 and 눕다 → 누워요.

dis.h: pick up dropped things from ground

p.n: 집다 stresses grasping with fingers; 줍다 stresses picking up something lying on the ground.

examples.en: Thanks to that student, I found my wallet.
Thanks to my friend, I finished moving quickly.
Thanks to my teacher, Korean is fun.
Thanks to the nice weather, I went for a walk.

examples.ko: 요즘 잘 지내요? — 네, 덕분에 잘 지내요.
examples.en: Are you doing well these days? — Yes, I'm doing well, thanks.

explain: 덕분에는 좋은 결과가 나왔을 때만 써요. 나쁜 결과에는 ‘때문에’를 써요: 비 때문에 늦었어요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 도움을 받아서 아주 고마울 때 조금 과장해서 하는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: a slightly exaggerated way to thank someone when their help was a big relief

dict_examples.ko: 선생님 덕분에 대학 생활을 무사히 마칠 수 있었습니다.
dict_examples.en: Thanks to my teacher, I was able to finish university life safely.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.en: Thanks to you, I had a good look.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 제가 잘된 것은 모두 형님 덕분입니다.
dict_examples.en: My success is all thanks to you, big brother.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 그동안 걱정해 준 덕분에 잘 지냈습니다.
dict_examples.en: Thanks to your concern, I have been doing well.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: 덕분에 is only for good results. For a bad result, use 때문에: 비 때문에 늦었어요 (I was late because of the rain).

en: to get, to obtain (often for free)

examples.en: I got a free cake at the shop where I work part-time.
I got two days off from work.
I got some useful information from my friend.
I drew a lot of strength from this book.
After graduating from university, I got a job.

explain: ‘얻다’는 돈을 주고 사는 게 아니라, 부탁하거나 노력해서 생길 때 써요. 선물은 ‘받다’를 써요.

dict_examples.en: to take out a loan from a bank
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.en: to get a job at the market
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.en: to gain life wisdom from travel
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 친구에게서 중요한 정보를 얻어 위기를 극복할 수 있었다.
dict_examples.en: I got important information from a friend and was able to overcome the crisis.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 거실에 놓을 의자 하나를 이웃집에서 얻었다.
dict_examples.en: I got a chair for the living room from a neighbor.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 영칠이는 담배 한 개비를 얻어 느긋하게 물고 피워댄다.
dict_examples.en: Yeongchil gets a cigarette and puffs on it leisurely.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: 얻다 is for getting something by asking or by effort, not by paying for it. A gift is 받다.

dis.h: get something from someone, often free

p.n: The other verb is formal and sounds odd for getting a book from a friend.

en: to remain, to be left over

examples.en: If there's food left over, you can take it to your room.
By the end of the month, I had no money left.
There are ten minutes left in the test.
Is there any rice left? — Yes, a little is left.
I stayed home and did my homework.

explain: 남다는 쓰고 나서 남은 것이 주어예요. 사람이 일부러 남기면 ‘남기다’를 써요: 밥을 남기지 마세요.

phrases.example: 여행에서 남는 건 사진뿐이니까 많이 찍어요.
phrases.en: photos are all you'll have left (so take lots)
phrases.nuance_ko: 사진을 많이 찍자고 할 때 자주 하는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: what people say when urging each other to take lots of photos on a trip
phrases.en_equiv: photos are all you'll have left (so take lots)

dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

dict_examples.ko: 시험 문제가 쉬워서 시험 시간이 남는다.
dict_examples.en: The exam questions are easy, so there's time left over.
dict_examples.src: 국립국어원 우리말샘 (CC BY-SA 2.0 KR) · 영어: AI 번역

explain_en: With 남다, the thing that is left over is the subject. When a person leaves something behind on purpose, use 남기다: 밥을 남기지 마세요 (Don't leave your rice).

dis.h: Be left over; also stay in place

p.n: 잔류하다 is formal and stresses staying behind while others leave.
